title: Heads Across Ten Coins
problem: Ten coins are flipped. Coin i has probability i/11 of landing heads, for i = 1, 2, ..., 10. The flips need not be independent. What is the expected total number of heads?

hints.text: Write the total number of heads as a sum of ten yes-or-no contributions.
If Xi indicates whether coin i is heads, then E[Xi] = i/11 and E[X1 + ... + X10] is the sum of those expectations.

solution.setup: Define Xi = 1 when coin i lands heads and Xi = 0 otherwise. Let H = X1 + ... + X10.
solution.reasoning: By linearity of expectation, E[H] = sum from i=1 to 10 of E[Xi] = sum from i=1 to 10 of i/11. The numerator is 1+2+...+10 = 55, so E[H] = 55/11. Independence is unnecessary because only the marginal probability of each head enters its individual expectation.
solution.sanityCheck: The probabilities pair to one: 1/11+10/11, 2/11+9/11, and so on. Five such pairs give expected total 5.

keyInsight: Expectation distributes over a sum even when the summands are dependent.
recognitionCues: The question asks for an expected total count and gives an individual probability for each contribution.
commonMistakes: Trying to determine a joint distribution or assuming independence is required.
followUps: Would the answer change if exactly one of each paired coins i and 11-i were guaranteed to land heads?

source.notes: Original exercise designed to make the non-independence point explicit.
